decision: Ordinary startup-only shared ATen runtime intra-op limit control and cold scope-correct reporting. Existing caller/executor/ggml per-invocation budgets retained; no per-context/per-replay process setter or aggregate live-OS-thread cap.

finite_fix.scope: Startup-only cpu::configure_runtime_threads(uint32) and cold runtime_thread_info POD; native implementation/helper in existing aten_cpu_provider.cc / torch_cpu_program.h, public conversion in cpu_context.cc.
requirements: Guard/requested state belongs to the actual HYLE native code image. One shared native library shares it; independent statically embedded HYLE facade/DSO copies do not, even if a Torch DLL is shared. Sibling HYLE copies are foreign users, coordinated by application before any use.

Before configuration or first use, report compiled availability/backend and UNKNOWN limits without calling ATen getters. After successful configure or a closed first-use window, report current-caller runtime limits, not live thread count.

Application must configure before all external ATen/OMP users and sibling HYLE images; foreign prior initialization cannot be detected or rolled back generally. Report requested separately from observed; foreign drift is visible, not enforced.
0 or >INT_MAX InvalidArgument; disabled configure Unimplemented and report unavailable/unknown. Interop is report-only; HYLE does not schedule work through ATen interop.

finite_fix.scope: One cold mutex serializes configure and first-use admission; freeze ordinary ATen context and Native prepare_torch_cpu before call_once warmup.
requirements: No mutex held across real math/replay. No per-context/per-replay setter/restore, no prepared/hot layout change.
Successful setter must be followed by getter equality before publishing requested. Native backend may only WARN on late resize; void return cannot prove application.

Conservatively close configuration after failed/partial setter or admitted first-use initialization attempt; requested remains UNKNOWN unless a prior successful setting existed. Do not promise rollback or reopen after partial runtime initialization.

Same-value idempotence requires a prior successful explicit request and matching observed limit, without setting again; a closed never-configured state cannot retroactively configure merely because its current limit matches. Different/late requests fail; foreign mismatch is report/refusal, not a repair setter.

finite_fix.scope: Original cold qualified_default_environment admission must reject explicit intraop !=1 and failed/partial state.
requirements: Preserve pre-existing unconfigured default behavior and original rule table/math/P1 identities.

Use the cold HYLE state snapshot for new admission; do not initialize ATen just to check a recipe. Validate complete context/prepare ordering so a recipe is not qualified before newly legal mutable configuration can change its premise.
This is respecting the existing qualification premise, not making a new performance claim or repairing G09 noise.

finite_fix.owner: compute_route_cpu + compute_provider_native and direct public consumers
finite_fix.scope: Finite meaningful API/race/disabled/bypass tests, CPU-only and CPU+GPU public sketches; selected Windows/WSL/Air source/static/shared CPU delivery plus featureOFF as root's planned gates.
requirements: Exercise same/different/late, invalid range, configuration vs first-use serialization, failed-set/observed mismatch, no early getter, disabled and Native low-precision bypass.

Two phase contexts and simultaneous invocations retain original output/error/retirement contracts. They share one immutable ATen limit within a native code-image domain, not two independently configured ATen phase pools.
Explicitly document caller masters, ggml per-invocation workers, borrowed executor, unknown vendor/background threads and application admission responsibility. No total-process thread cap asserted.
Do not introduce a P1 claim, change math/rule tables/thresholds or repeat unchanged full GPU delivery. Exact selected gates and owner audit remain parent's card responsibility.

nonclaims: No product code, native build, timing/GPU or acceptance in this snapshot. Three G09 failed AA qualifications remain separate; this is not a demonstrated G09 fix. No compatibility layer or new threadpool framework.
